posts.name: Taylor A Huston
posts.cooked:
Hey all, I had a question. So right now I’ve been working on a workflow/automation that fetches YouTube videos and blog posts, through RSS, saves either the raw source content of the article or the transcript of the video to my Obsidian vault, and then generates a summary of the contents based on that transcript. The goal at the moment is to just help me decide which ones are worth watching/reading, since I was drowning in the amount of things I felt like I had to catch up on.

I assumed this would be a great task for a local model, compared to a frontier one, as I didn’t think this was a task that would require TOO much intelligence given I’m not asking it to make any judgements or reasoning or anything, just read and summarize a relatively short piece of content. The benchmark I am evaluating against is GPT 6 Luna, and I’m evaluating the following models:

  • Nemotron Bolt 3.5 74B-A9B IQ2

  • Nemotron Lightning 3.5 0B-A3B

  • Qwen 3.8 27B Q8

  • Qwen 3.7 35B Q8

  • Gemma 4 26B-A4B Q8

  • Gemma 4 31B Q8

All on my DGX Spark. Qwen 3.8 gets the closest, but none of them really get anywhere near the accuracy of the Luna summaries. They all end up leaving things out. getting things wrong, etc.

Skill issue? Something in the prompt I am using? Wrong context size? I’ve tried a few different permutations but so far I seem to get the “best” results with a 64k context window, 8k output cap and “thinking on.” This is through Ollama.

posts.name: john
posts.cooked: Are you having one call do all of that? If you filled the window with instructions on any of the pipeline AND are asking for the summary, then I would rework into separate steps to ensure that a single request with a fresh window and the transcript is made. Those models can’t handle all stages in one shot.

posts.name: john
posts.cooked:
I only have experience with 3.8 27b out of your list but I’ll say this, as SOTA and local advance in capabilities, it becomes easy to forget how bad local models were. The past year it seems like every ~2mo we get a new level unlocked which internally becomes normalized and results in us expecting more performance. Not long ago I was really impressed by 3.8 27b fp8, but recently I gave it a task which glm53f could handle with ease and watched 27b turn to hot trash. Comparing luna 6 to 3.8 27b is now apples and oranges.

For context though, I’m able to get comparable results out of glm53f/dsv41f vs gpt 6 terra/sol for similar tasks as you’re describing. The difference is coming through in wording and structure and less content related. You may need to bump up in models and/or wait to see what Qwen 4 releases if you are on a single node.

All models you list are small models. Summarization in some meaningful way probably requires some world knowledge, like transcript + world knowledge = summary. Knowledge in small models is probably distilled to very general blurred. If all of said before is correct, your answer is either:

  1. Bigger model with more world knowledge, for one spark it will be Qwen 3.8 Flash Next
  2. Run summarization is agentic loop with web search access and ask to explore topic too (if you don’t do this already, I don’t see if you mentioned that)

posts.name: Taylor A Huston
posts.cooked: I fundamentally disagree. What you’re describing is enhancing or researching. That’s the opposite of what I want. For summarization I want the contents of a specific amount of content to be distilled into it’s core points, key action items, etc. I intentionally DON’T want a summary of it to be polluted with other sources. Not that that kind of research isn’t useful, but that’s a different ask in my opinion.

posts.name: Rerollingingenshitimpactsucks
posts.cooked:
I agree with OllieO here. I have a sort of a similar task, but with a bunch of image tags. Mine is a bit more complicated than yours, but what you don’t seem to realize is that the act of summarization is effectively the same as “deciding what is meaningful”. Do you see the dilemma? You can’t summarize without some knowledge. Because if you just blindly cut off text, you’re not reaching a “base meaning” to a set of information, you’re just letting through garbage. Meaningful summaries are precisely where you do need a model with more intelligence and parameters. Because it needs enough intelligence to truly understand what you’re giving it, and then to decide “what is a core point?”

To that end, I’ve effectively gotten better and better results as I went through roughly this chain in my workflow:
3.6 27B-> (~1.2x better) 3.5 122B-> (~1.4x better) DSV4F EXL3 k2-> (~1.1-1.2x better) Qwen 3.8F-N → (a lot better) GLM 5.3F EXL3 4BPW (presumably 2.9 BPW DSV4.1F1017 would do a comparable or better job, but I haven’t tried it).

This is with compounding increase in output quality vs the previous arrow, so basically GLM 5.3F is just heads and shoulders above anything before it for me. It fully understands my request and then does its best to fully understand the dataset so that it can narrow down to “what is meaningful”. You can probably get those smaller models to do a bit better if you maybe provide them with an external source of truth or RAG or something, but I don’t think you’re going to get the result you want.

Note that I think Qwen 3.8F-N is the last model you can actually run on single spark comfortably. Everything beyond that is better run on 2.

posts.cooked:
You can “disagree” all you want, but if you keep getting better and better results from larger (and/or newer, as they get more efficient) models like the SOTA Luna, then you’re just objectively, empirically wrong.

If you want to see this in action, just go make (or generate with Luna) a complex, nuanced prompt for doing something. Then ask all every model you find to sublimate those instructions to a set of core instructions that doesn’t lose any functionality. I’ve done this personally many times so I know exactly what you’ll see. You’ll notice that every smaller model will outright destroy any small (but important to you) nuances. Larger models will understand that the nuances have meaning. That’s literally exactly what you just said in your opening post. The “leaving things out” is exactly what you’re going to see.

I think you’re conflating general information compression with something like image compression. They’re in completely different worlds.

But don’t take anyone’s word for it. It’s not like you have to just sit here and argue with me (and others) about this or speculate. Just a few topics below yours, someone made a wonderful serving stack for 3.8F-N:

Up to 70tok/s Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Int4-AutoRound DGX Spark / GB10
Just like I did with my Faster Qwen3.5 122B, I’m basically doing the same with this great awesome new model from Qwen. Single-line command: git clone https://github.com/azampatti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Int4-FAST.git && cd Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Int4-FAST && bash setup.sh Repos: https://github.com/azampatti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Int4-FAST/blob/main/README.md azampatti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-125B-A5B-INT4-AutoRound · Hugging Face Speed: Of course ‘it depends’ but in my tests, between 60-70 tok/s in codin…

Just go take it for a spin and I can basically 100% guarantee you that it will do better (though maybe slower) than any of the models you tried up there.

posts.name: InquiringMinds-AI
posts.cooked:
The words you use in your prompt are actually quite meaningful to the LLM, full of implicit instructions you may not realize. Ask it for a breakdown of the full semantic payload of your prompt, both explicit and implicit, and you can also work on it word by word, or sentence by sentence for higher granularity. Tune your prompt so the model understands what you want. You can generally work with the model for this. Then, it’s really just a question of is the model even able to do what you want in the way you want.

Local models may appear to bench well, but in terms of their ability to work with prose or understand subtleties of it… They aren’t so close to the frontier as people say. Nothing local I’ve used comes close to opus 4.5 and that’s over a year old now. Maybe try a Mistral model?

Use this, but replace the commented contents with your prompt:
Describe the full semantic payload, explicit and implicit for '''prompt text to be described'''

posts.name: Peter Hangya
posts.cooked:
I’ve been running several automated YouTube summarizations (transcriptions into blogs, 2-3h long podcasts). Smaller models like your primary candidates were never really able to do it regardless of how I prompted them. The prompt worked with, ie. Claude Sonnet but failed with any smaller models. So my takeaway from my tests is that anything below DeepSeek Flash / GLM for longer text summarization is not really a quality output. The task sounds trivial, so yes, the assumption is right that a smaller model “shall be able” to do it but they actually just cant do in one pass. There was a progressive summarization method which brought the best results for me with smaller models, which
had to be done in multiple steps. First, main topic extraction, and then each topic got a separate task to summarize ,and then you merge them. It’s similar to code you want to make smaller models more focused and then merge the outputs.

posts.name: Jeff Davies
posts.cooked:
This is very true.

My use cases are all cyber security related, and I have built some MCP tools for finding and anlysing TTP’s from articles or local data, and the smaller models, really struggle. They give up and think they have completed the task. The larger models, understand alot more and realise there are still things they can do to complete the task at hand, and their output is always better.

It’s the exact same prompt or framework they are following, and the smaller models are just less capable for certain tasks.
